title: Classic Spaghetti Carbonara
description: Spaghetti in a glossy sauce of eggs, Pecorino Romano, crisp guanciale, and plenty of black pepper. There is no cream; the silkiness comes from tempering the eggs with hot pasta water.
notes: Contains eggs, milk, and wheat. The eggs in carbonara are only gently cooked by the residual heat of the pasta and are not brought to a fully cooked temperature. Anyone who should avoid undercooked eggs (people who are pregnant, older adults, young children, and anyone with a weakened immune system) should use pasteurized eggs or choose another dish. Never put the sauce back over direct heat or it will scramble. Guanciale (cured pork cheek) is traditional; pancetta or thick-cut unsmoked bacon are good substitutes. The only added salt is in the pasta water, because the pork and cheese are salty; the water quantity is deliberately small so it is extra starchy. Carbonara is best eaten right away. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day, reheating gently in a skillet with a splash of water; the sauce will be less silky.

ingredients.name: kosher salt, for the pasta water
guanciale or pancetta, cut into 1/4-inch-thick batons
Pecorino Romano, finely grated (about 1 cup), plus more to serve
coarsely ground black pepper, plus more to serve

instructions: Bring about 3 quarts of water to a boil in a large pot over high heat and stir in the kosher salt. This is less water than usual on purpose: the starchier it is, the better it binds the sauce.

While the water heats, put the guanciale in a cold 12-inch skillet and set it over medium-low heat. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the fat has rendered and the pieces are golden and crisp at the edges but still a little chewy. Turn off the heat and leave the guanciale and about 3 tablespoons of its fat in the pan, spooning off any extra.
In a large heatproof bowl, whisk the eggs, egg yolks, Pecorino Romano, Parmesan, and black pepper into a thick, smooth paste.

Cook the spaghetti in the boiling water, stirring occasionally, until al dente, usually about 1 minute less than the package time. Just before it is done, ladle out 1 cup of the pasta water and keep the pot of hot water on the stove with the heat off.

Temper the eggs: whisking the egg mixture constantly, drizzle in 1/4 cup of the hot pasta water a little at a time. This warms the eggs gradually and loosens the paste, so they thicken into a sauce instead of seizing when they meet the hot pasta.

Use tongs to lift the spaghetti straight from the pot into the skillet with the guanciale, heat still off, and toss for 30 seconds to coat it in the fat and let it cool very slightly. Scrape the pasta, guanciale, and fat into the bowl of tempered eggs.

Toss vigorously with the tongs for 1 to 2 minutes, adding more pasta water 1 to 2 tablespoons at a time, until the sauce turns creamy and glossy and clings to the strands with no runny egg pooled in the bowl. If it stays thin, rest the bowl over the pot of hot water and keep tossing for 30 to 60 seconds until it thickens; if it tightens up, add another splash of pasta water.
Divide among warmed bowls and serve immediately with extra Pecorino Romano and black pepper.

title: Weeknight Beef Bolognese with Rigatoni
description: A bolognese-style meat sauce that fits a weeknight: ground beef, soft vegetables, wine, tomatoes, and a splash of milk simmered until thick, then tossed with rigatoni so it fills every tube.
equipment: Dutch oven or large deep skillet
notes: Contains milk and wheat. Use dried durum wheat rigatoni, which is made without egg; fresh pasta usually contains egg. Ground beef is safely cooked at 160°F; it passes that point well before the sauce is done. The milk softens the acidity of the tomatoes and keeps the meat tender, so do not skip it. No wine: use 1/2 cup beef broth plus 1 teaspoon red wine vinegar. Half beef and half ground pork also works well. The pasta-water salt is listed for a pot of about 4 quarts and most of it goes down the drain. The sauce (without pasta) keeps 4 days in the refrigerator and 3 months in the freezer; cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours. Reheat until bubbling, loosening with a splash of water.

ingredients.name: medium carrot, peeled and finely diced
kosher salt, for the pasta water

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a Dutch oven or large deep skillet over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, celery, and 1/2 teaspoon of the fine salt and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are soft and just starting to turn golden. Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.

Raise the heat to medium-high and add the ground beef. Cook for 7 to 9 minutes, breaking it into small pieces with a wooden spoon, until no pink remains (160°F), the liquid has cooked off, and the meat is sizzling in its fat and starting to brown.

Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, until it darkens to brick red and begins to stick to the pot. Pour in the wine and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, until almost all of it has evaporated.

Add the crushed tomatoes, milk, bay leaf, black pepper, and remaining 3/4 teaspoon fine salt. Bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low, partially cover, and cook for 30 to 35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick and a spoon dragged across the bottom leaves a trail. Add a splash of water if it thickens too quickly.

During the last 15 minutes of simmering, bring a large pot of water (about 4 quarts) to a boil over high heat and add the kosher salt. Cook the rigatoni until 1 minute short of the package time, so it is still firm in the center. Scoop out 1 cup of the pasta water, then drain.

Discard the bay leaf. Add the rigatoni, half of the Parmesan, and 1/4 cup of the pasta water to the sauce and toss over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes, until the sauce clings to the pasta and fills the tubes. Loosen with more pasta water a splash at a time if it looks dry.
Taste and adjust the salt, then serve topped with the remaining Parmesan.

title: Baked Macaroni and Cheese with Crisp Panko Topping
description: Elbow macaroni in a smooth sharp cheddar and Gruyère sauce, baked under buttered panko until bubbling at the edges and golden on top.
notes: Contains milk and wheat. Grate the cheese yourself: pre-shredded cheese is coated with anti-caking starch and can make the sauce grainy. Taking the pot off the heat before adding the cheese also keeps the sauce smooth. Swap the Gruyère for Monterey Jack, fontina, or more cheddar. Dried elbow macaroni is made without egg, but check the label. Strict vegetarians should check that the cheeses are made with non-animal rennet. Let the baked dish rest 10 minutes before serving so the sauce settles. Make-ahead: assemble without the panko, cover, and refrigerate up to 24 hours; add the panko and bake for 35 to 40 minutes, covering with foil for the first 15. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours; they keep 4 days. Reheat covered at 350°F for 15 to 20 minutes with a splash of milk stirred in.

ingredients.name: kosher salt, for the pasta water
unsalted butter, plus a little for the dish
sharp cheddar cheese, coarsely grated (about 3 cups)

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F and lightly butter a 9x13-inch (3-quart) baking dish. Bring a large pot of water (about 4 quarts) to a boil over high heat, add the kosher salt, and cook the macaroni for 2 minutes less than the package time, until bendable but still quite firm; it finishes cooking in the oven. Drain well and do not rinse.

Return the empty pot to medium heat and melt the 5 tablespoons butter. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, whisking constantly, until the paste is foamy and smells toasty but is still pale.

Pour in the milk about 1 cup at a time, whisking until smooth after each addition. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, whisking often and scraping the corners of the pot, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon and a finger drawn through it leaves a clean line.

Take the pot off the heat and whisk in the mustard, smoked paprika, fine salt, and black pepper. Toss the two cheeses together and set aside 1 cup for the top. Add the rest to the sauce a handful at a time, stirring until each addition melts and the sauce is smooth.
Fold the drained macaroni into the sauce. It will look loose, which is right: the pasta absorbs sauce as it bakes. Scrape into the baking dish and scatter the reserved cheese over the top.
Stir the panko with the melted butter until evenly moistened, then sprinkle it over the cheese in an even layer.
Bake on the middle rack for 20 to 25 minutes, until the sauce is bubbling around the edges and the crumbs are deep golden. Let stand for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Pasta e Ceci (One-Pot Pasta with Chickpeas)
description: A thick Italian stew of chickpeas and small pasta cooked together in a garlicky tomato and rosemary broth. Crushing some of the chickpeas makes it creamy without any dairy.
equipment: Large heavy pot or Dutch oven
notes: Vegan and nut-free as written; contains wheat. Dried ditalini is normally made without egg, but check the label. Any small shape works: tubetti, small shells, or spaghetti broken into short pieces. The pasta cooks directly in the broth, so there is no separate pasta water to salt; broths vary in saltiness, so taste before adding more at the end. The stew thickens a lot as it sits. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 4 days; reheat over medium-low heat with enough water or broth to loosen it. The pasta will be softer on day two. A gluten-free small pasta can be used, but start checking it 2 minutes early.

ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to drizzle
fine sea salt, divided, plus more to taste
(15 oz each) chickpeas, drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and translucent. Add the garlic, rosemary sprig, and red pepper flakes and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant but not browned.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until it darkens to brick red and starts to stick to the bottom of the pot.

Add the chickpeas, vegetable broth, water, and remaining 3/4 teaspoon salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 10 minutes. Use the back of the spoon or a potato masher to crush about one third of the chickpeas against the side of the pot, which thickens the broth.

Raise the heat to medium so the pot is at a steady simmer and stir in the ditalini. Cook for 9 to 11 minutes, stirring often so the pasta does not stick to the bottom, until the pasta is tender and the broth has thickened into a loose, creamy stew. Add a splash of hot water if it becomes too thick before the pasta is done.
Take the pot off the heat, pull out the rosemary stem, and stir in the black pepper and lemon juice. Let it stand for 3 minutes to thicken slightly, then taste and add more salt if needed.
Ladle into bowls and finish each with a drizzle of olive oil and the parsley.

title: Chicken Pad Thai with Tamarind and Peanuts
description: Chewy rice noodles stir-fried with chicken, egg, and bean sprouts in a sweet, sour, and salty sauce of tamarind and fish sauce, finished with roasted peanuts and lime.
notes: Contains fish sauce (fish), peanuts, and eggs. The noodles need a 25 to 30 minute soak, which is not counted in the cook time; use it to prep everything else. Do not boil the noodles or they will turn mushy in the pan. Tamarind: this recipe uses the pourable Thai-style concentrate sometimes labeled cooking tamarind. Thick, dark Indian-style concentrate is much stronger; use 1 tablespoon mixed with 2 tablespoons water instead. This amount is the most a home burner can stir-fry well; to serve more, cook a second batch rather than doubling. Gluten-free as written, but check the labels on the fish sauce and tamarind. For a peanut allergy, leave out the peanuts and use toasted sunflower seeds. Raw sprouts carry a higher food-safety risk; if serving anyone pregnant, elderly, very young, or immune-compromised, stir all of the sprouts into the hot pan. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days, reheating in a skillet with a splash of water.

ingredients.name: dried flat rice noodles (about 1/4 inch wide)
light brown sugar or palm sugar, packed
boneless, skinless chicken thighs, thinly sliced across the grain
neutral oil such as canola or avocado, divided
roasted unsalted peanuts, roughly chopped, divided

instructions: Put the rice noodles in a large bowl and cover with hot tap water (not boiling). Soak for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring once to separate them, until they are pliable enough to wrap around a finger but still firm and opaque white in the center. Drain well.

While the noodles soak, stir the fish sauce, tamarind, sugar, and water in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves; it should taste sharply sour, salty, and sweet in roughly equal measure. Toss the chicken with the salt. Set every ingredient next to the stove, because the cooking moves fast.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large wok or 12-inch nonstick skillet over high heat until shimmering. Add the chicken in a single layer and let it sear for 1 minute, then stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes, until browned and cooked through (165°F). Transfer to a plate.

Reduce the heat to medium-high and add another 1 tablespoon oil. Stir-fry the shallot and garlic for 30 to 45 seconds, until fragrant and pale gold. Add the drained noodles and the sauce and toss constantly for 2 to 3 minutes, until the noodles have absorbed most of the sauce and are tender but still chewy. If the pan is dry and the noodles are still stiff, add 2 tablespoons water and keep tossing.

Push the noodles to one side of the pan and pour the remaining 1 tablespoon oil into the empty side. Crack in the eggs, break the yolks, and let them set for 30 seconds, then scramble for about 1 minute, until just firm. Fold the eggs into the noodles.

Return the chicken to the pan and add half of the bean sprouts, the scallions, and half of the peanuts. Toss over medium-high heat for 30 to 60 seconds, until the scallions wilt and the sprouts are barely softened.
Serve immediately, topped with the remaining bean sprouts and peanuts, with lime wedges to squeeze over and red pepper flakes if you like heat.

title: Chicken Fried Rice with Egg and Vegetables
description: Day-old jasmine rice stir-fried over high heat with seared chicken, soft scrambled egg, peas, carrots, and scallions. Tamari keeps it gluten-free.
notes: Contains eggs, soy, and sesame. Gluten-free only if the tamari is labeled gluten-free; regular soy sauce contains wheat. Cold, dry rice is what keeps the grains separate, so cook it ahead: 1 1/3 cups uncooked jasmine rice gives about 4 cups cooked. Spread the hot rice on a tray to cool quickly, refrigerate it within 1 hour of cooking, and use it within 2 days. Never use rice that has been sitting out at room temperature. Same-day shortcut: spread freshly cooked rice on a baking sheet and refrigerate uncovered for 1 to 2 hours, until cold and dry to the touch. Refrigerate leftover fried rice within 1 hour, keep up to 3 days, and reheat once only, until steaming hot throughout (165°F). For a vegetable version, replace the chicken with 2 cups of diced vegetables such as bell pepper, corn, and mushrooms, and skip the cornstarch step.

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1/2-inch pieces
neutral oil such as canola or avocado, divided
scallions, thinly sliced, white and green parts separated
frozen peas and diced carrots, thawed
fine sea salt, plus more to taste

instructions: In a small bowl, toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon of the tamari and the cornstarch and set aside while you prepare the other ingredients. Crumble the cold rice with your fingers so there are no clumps.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large wok or 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Pour in the eggs and scramble for 45 to 60 seconds, until just set in soft curds. Transfer to a plate.

Raise the heat to high and add another 1 tablespoon oil. Spread the chicken in a single layer and sear without stirring for 1 minute, then stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes, until browned and cooked through (165°F). Add it to the plate with the eggs.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon oil to the pan, then the scallion whites, garlic, and ginger. Stir-fry for 30 seconds, until fragrant, then add the peas and carrots and cook for 1 minute, until hot.

Add the rice and spread it across the pan, pressing it against the hot surface. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, tossing every 30 seconds, until the grains are separate, steaming hot, and a few are lightly toasted.

Drizzle the remaining 2 tablespoons tamari around the edge of the pan, sprinkle in the salt and white pepper, and toss for 1 minute. Return the chicken and eggs to the pan, breaking the eggs into small pieces, and toss for 1 minute more, until everything is heated through.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the sesame oil and scallion greens. Taste, add a pinch more salt if needed, and serve right away.

title: One-Pot Chicken Biryani-Style Rice
description: Yogurt-marinated chicken thighs and basmati rice cooked together in one pot with deeply browned onions, warm spices, mint, and cilantro. A streamlined home take on layered biryani.
equipment: 5- to 6-quart Dutch oven with a tight lid
notes: Contains milk (yogurt and ghee). This is a one-pot shortcut, not a traditional layered dum biryani, but it keeps the same flavors. The rice soaks for 30 minutes and the chicken marinates for the same time (or up to 8 hours in the refrigerator); neither is counted in the cook time. Soaking matters: the water quantity is set for soaked, well-drained basmati. Use a heavy pot and your smallest burner on its lowest setting so the bottom does not scorch; a thin golden crust on the bottom is normal. The cinnamon stick and cardamom pods are for flavor only, so pick them out or warn the table. For a dairy-free version use unsweetened coconut yogurt and oil. Serve with cucumber raita or sliced cucumber and lemon wedges. Cooked rice should not sit out: refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour in shallow containers, keep up to 3 days, and reheat until steaming hot throughout (165°F).

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
Kashmiri chili powder (or 3/4 tsp sweet paprika plus 1/4 tsp cayenne)
large yellow onions, halved and thinly sliced
fresh cilantro and mint leaves, roughly chopped, divided

instructions: Rinse the rice in a bowl of cold water, swishing and draining 3 or 4 times, until the water is nearly clear. Cover with fresh cold water and soak for 30 minutes, then drain well in a fine-mesh strainer. Meanwhile, in a large bowl, mix the chicken with the yogurt, ginger, garlic, garam masala, chili powder, turmeric, and 1 teaspoon of the salt, and leave it to marinate while the rice soaks.

Heat the ghee in a 5- to 6-quart Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onions and cook for 15 to 18 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden brown and sweet; lower the heat if the edges darken too quickly. Lift out half of the onions and set them aside for serving.

Add the cinnamon stick and cardamom pods to the onions left in the pot and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant. Raise the heat to medium-high, add the chicken with all of its marinade, and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring often, until the chicken is opaque on the outside and the sauce has thickened and looks glossy at the edges.
Add the drained rice, the water, the remaining 1 1/4 teaspoons salt, and half of the cilantro and mint. Stir gently once, scraping the bottom of the pot so nothing is stuck, and bring to a full boil.
Cover with a tight-fitting lid (lay a sheet of foil under the lid if it is loose), reduce the heat to the lowest setting, and cook for 18 minutes without lifting the lid.
Turn off the heat and let the pot stand, still covered, for 10 minutes. The water should be fully absorbed, the rice tender with separate grains, and the chicken cooked through to at least 165°F.

Sprinkle the lemon juice over the rice and fluff gently with a fork, working in from the edges and lifting the chicken up from the bottom. Top with the reserved browned onions and the remaining cilantro and mint, and serve hot.

title: Mushroom Risotto with Thyme and Parmesan
description: Arborio rice stirred with hot broth until creamy, then folded with deeply browned mushrooms, thyme, butter, and Parmesan. Naturally gluten-free, with a simple vegan swap in the notes.
equipment: Wide heavy pot or Dutch oven
notes: Contains milk. To make it vegan: cook the mushrooms and shallot in olive oil only, finish with 2 tablespoons olive oil or dairy-free butter in place of the butter, and replace the Parmesan with 2 tablespoons nutritional yeast; check that the wine is vegan-friendly. Gluten-free as written, but check the broth label. Strict vegetarians should use a Parmesan-style cheese made with non-animal rennet. Do not rinse the rice; its surface starch is what makes the risotto creamy. Keep the broth hot so each addition does not stall the cooking, and expect to use 5 to 5 1/2 cups; any extra is for loosening at the end. A mix of cremini and shiitake caps is especially good. No wine: use extra broth and add 1 more teaspoon lemon juice at the end. Risotto is best fresh. Cool leftovers quickly, refrigerate within 1 hour, keep up to 2 days, and reheat with a splash of broth until steaming hot.

ingredients.name: fine sea salt, divided, plus more to taste
Parmesan, finely grated (about 1 cup), plus more to serve

instructions: Bring the broth to a bare simmer in a medium saucepan, then keep it hot over low heat.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the olive oil and 1 tablespoon of the butter in a wide heavy pot over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms in an even layer and cook without stirring for 3 minutes, then cook for 5 to 7 minutes more, stirring occasionally, until their liquid has evaporated and they are deeply browned. Stir in 1/2 teaspoon of the salt and the thyme, then transfer to a bowl.

Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil and 1 more tablespoon butter to the pot. Cook the shallot for 3 minutes, until soft and translucent, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds. Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes, until the edges of the grains look translucent and it smells lightly toasted.
Pour in the wine and stir for about 1 minute, until it is almost completely absorbed.

Add the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and a ladleful of hot broth (about 3/4 cup). Keep the pot at a lively simmer and stir frequently, adding another ladleful each time the last is mostly absorbed and the spoon leaves a clear trail on the bottom. Continue for 18 to 22 minutes, until the rice is tender with a slight bite in the center and the risotto flows when you shake the pot.

Take the pot off the heat. Add the mushrooms, the last 1 tablespoon butter, the Parmesan, black pepper, and lemon juice and beat vigorously with the spoon for 30 seconds, until creamy. Stir in a splash more broth if needed so it spreads slowly on a plate rather than holding a mound, then cover and let rest for 2 minutes.
Taste and adjust the salt. Spoon into warm bowls and top with the parsley and extra Parmesan.

title: Vegetable Lo Mein with Shiitake Mushrooms
description: Springy egg noodles tossed in a hot pan with browned shiitakes, cabbage, carrot, and bell pepper in a savory soy and sesame sauce. On the table faster than takeout.
notes: Contains wheat, eggs, soy, and sesame. Lo mein noodles are made with wheat and egg; if you cannot find them, use 8 ounces of spaghetti or linguine cooked to al dente, which also makes the dish egg-free and vegan. Many restaurant versions include oyster sauce; it is left out here so the dish stays vegetarian and shellfish-free. Dark soy sauce adds color and a faint molasses sweetness; if you do not have it, use 2 more teaspoons of regular soy sauce. Have everything cut and the sauce mixed before you turn on the heat, and keep the pan hot so the vegetables sear instead of steaming. To add protein, stir-fry 8 ounces of pressed tofu or thinly sliced chicken first (chicken to 165°F), set aside, and return it with the noodles. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and keep up to 3 days; reheat in a hot skillet with a splash of water.

ingredients.name: soy sauce, plus more to taste
fresh lo mein egg noodles (or 8 oz dried)
neutral oil such as canola or avocado, divided
medium carrot, peeled and cut into thin matchsticks
green or napa cabbage, thinly sliced

instructions: In a small bowl, stir together the soy sauce, dark soy sauce, sesame oil, water, sugar, and white pepper until the sugar dissolves.

Bring a large pot of unsalted water to a boil over high heat. Cook the noodles until just tender with some chew, 2 to 3 minutes for fresh or 4 to 6 minutes for dried. Drain, rinse briefly under cold water to stop the cooking, and shake the colander until the noodles are very dry.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large wok or 12-inch skillet over high heat until it just begins to smoke. Add the mushrooms and salt and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until browned and their moisture has cooked off.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon oil, then the carrot, bell pepper, and cabbage. Stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes, until the vegetables are crisp-tender and the cabbage has wilted with a few charred edges.
Clear a space in the center of the pan and add the garlic and ginger. Stir them there for 30 seconds, until fragrant, then mix them into the vegetables.

Add the noodles and pour the sauce over them. Toss with tongs for about 2 minutes, lifting from the bottom, until the noodles are evenly colored and hot and no liquid remains in the pan. Add the scallions for the last 30 seconds so they stay bright green.
Taste, add a small splash of soy sauce if it needs more salt, and serve immediately.

title: Greek-Style Orzo Salad with Feta and Chickpeas
description: Orzo, chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes, olives, and feta in a lemon and oregano vinaigrette. It holds up for days in the refrigerator, which makes it good for lunches and picnics.
notes: Contains wheat and milk. Orzo is a small wheat pasta, not a grain; a gluten-free orzo can be substituted. Rinsing the orzo is intentional here: it cools the pasta fast and washes off the surface starch that would make a cold salad gummy. Dressing the orzo while it is still slightly damp helps it absorb the vinaigrette. Keeps up to 4 days in the refrigerator in a covered container; the orzo soaks up dressing as it sits, so refresh it with a squeeze of lemon and a drizzle of olive oil before serving. If you are making it more than a day ahead, add the cucumber and tomatoes on the day you serve it so they stay crisp. Do not leave the salad out for more than 2 hours (1 hour in hot weather). For a vegan version, leave out the feta, add an extra 1/4 cup olives, and season with a little more salt. Strict vegetarians should check that the feta is made with non-animal rennet.

ingredients.name: kosher salt, for the pasta water
fine sea salt, plus more to taste

instructions: Bring a large pot of water (about 4 quarts) to a boil over high heat and add the kosher salt. Add the orzo, stir well for the first minute so it does not stick to the bottom, and cook until al dente according to the package time, usually 8 to 10 minutes.
While the orzo cooks, whisk the olive oil, vinegar, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, fine salt, and black pepper in a large mixing bowl until blended.
Drain the orzo in a fine-mesh strainer and rinse under cold running water for 20 to 30 seconds, tossing, until cool to the touch. Shake the strainer well to remove as much water as possible.
Add the orzo, chickpeas, and red onion to the bowl of dressing and toss to coat. Let stand for 10 minutes so the pasta and chickpeas absorb the dressing and the onion mellows.
Fold in the cucumber, tomatoes, olives, parsley, and about two thirds of the feta, mixing gently so the cheese stays in pieces.
Taste and adjust with more salt or a squeeze of lemon. Scatter the remaining feta over the top and serve at cool room temperature, or cover and chill until needed.
